verdict: Visa's net revenue rose 10% to $8.9B as payments volume grew 7% and cross-border volume 14% — and with last year's large legal provision not repeating, net income jumped 17% to $4.9B.

segments.name: Service revenue
segments.note: Fees based on the payments volume Visa's clients processed in the prior quarter.

segments.name: Data processing revenue
segments.note: Fees for authorizing, clearing and settling each transaction on Visa's network.

segments.name: International transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees when a card is used outside its home country — the cross-border business.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Value-added services, consulting and other fees.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Salaries and benefits for the people who run the network.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — offices, legal and administration.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and sponsorships that keep the Visa brand in front of cardholders.

opex.name: Litigation provision
opex.note: Setting money aside for legal cases (see one-time items).

opex.name: Network, professional & depreciation
opex.note: Running the network, outside professional help, and wear on Visa's technology — $200M network and processing, $152M professional fees and $264M depreciation and amortization.

otherDetail: Investment income and other income of $247M, partly offset by $196M of interest expense on Visa's debt.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $8,900M; this page starts from gross revenue of $12,430M so the $3,530M of client incentives shows as a cost.

takeaways.title: Cross-border stayed hot
takeaways.text: Payments volume rose 7% in constant dollars and processed transactions 10% to 59.3 billion, while cross-border volume — the most lucrative traffic — jumped 14%, lifting international transaction revenue 9%.

takeaways.title: Every revenue line grew
takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 10% to $8,900M: service revenue +8%, data processing +9%, international transaction +9% and other revenue +31%, against client incentives of $3,530M paid back to card issuers.

takeaways.title: Profit grew faster than revenue
takeaways.text: Net income rose 17% to $4,872M and EPS 20% to $2.40 — helped by a litigation provision of just $13M versus $457M a year ago. Excluding special items, non-GAAP EPS was $2.42.

oneTimers: GAAP results include three special items: a $118M release of an indirect tax reserve set aside in fiscal 2021 (a gain), a $67M donation of investment securities to the Visa Foundation, and a $10M litigation provision for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case. Excluding these and related items, non-GAAP net income was $4,909M, or $2.42 per share.
